overview.one_sentence: DeepSeek-V3 introduces a 671B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model with auxiliary-loss-free load balancing and multi-token prediction, achieving cost-efficient training and state-of-the-art performance on open-source benchmarks.
overview.problem: Large language models face bottlenecks in training efficiency, expert load imbalance, and high computational costs, limiting scalability and performance gains despite architectural advancements.
overview.solution: DeepSeek-V3 employs Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA), DeepSeekMoE with auxiliary-loss-free load balancing, multi-token prediction training, and FP8 mixed-precision training to optimize inference, training stability, and cost-effectiveness.
overview.why_it_matters: DeepSeek-V3 achieves competitive performance with closed-source models while reducing training costs to 2.788M H800 GPU hours, demonstrating scalable and efficient large-model training with minimal performance trade-offs.

contributions.title: Auxiliary-Loss-Free Load Balancing in DeepSeekMoE
contributions.summary: Introduces a bias-based dynamic adjustment mechanism to balance expert load without auxiliary loss, mitigating performance degradation while maintaining computational efficiency.
contributions.importance: Eliminates trade-offs between load balancing and model performance, enabling stable MoE training at scale.

contributions.title: Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) Training Objective
contributions.summary: Sequentially predicts multiple future tokens per position, densifying training signals and improving data efficiency while preserving causal chains for better future token planning.
contributions.importance: Enhances model performance on benchmarks and enables speculative decoding for inference acceleration.

contributions.title: FP8 Mixed-Precision Training Framework
contributions.summary: Validates FP8 training for large-scale models (671B parameters) with fine-grained quantization and increased accumulation precision, reducing memory and compute costs by ~50%.
contributions.importance: Achieves stable training with <0.25% relative loss error compared to BF16, enabling cost-effective scaling of model sizes.

contributions.title: DualPipe Pipeline Parallelism
contributions.summary: Overlaps forward/backward computation-communication phases to reduce pipeline bubbles and near-zero all-to-all communication overhead, supporting fine-grained expert parallelism across nodes.
contributions.importance: Enables efficient training of large models without costly tensor parallelism, maintaining scalability with constant computation-to-communication ratios.

contributions.title: Efficient Cross-Node All-to-All Communication
contributions.summary: Leverages InfiniBand (IB) and NVLink bandwidths with warp specialization and dynamic workload balancing, reducing communication overhead to 20 SMs while scaling expert parallelism.
contributions.importance: Supports near-full computation-communication overlap, enabling 13 routed experts per node without additional overhead.

key_findings.title: MMLU-Pro Benchmark Performance
key_findings.summary: DeepSeek-V3 achieves 75.9% Exact Match (EM) on MMLU-Pro, outperforming all open-source models and narrowing the gap with closed-source models like GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet.

key_findings.title: Math and Code Benchmark Dominance
key_findings.summary: State-of-the-art performance on math (MATH 500: 90.2 EM) and code benchmarks (LiveCodeBench: top-performing model), surpassing closed-source models like o1-preview on specific tasks.

key_findings.title: Training Efficiency and Cost
key_findings.summary: Pre-training completed in 2.664M H800 GPU hours (~3.7 days per trillion tokens) with total training cost of $5.576M, achieving stable training without irrecoverable loss spikes.

key_findings.title: FP8 Training Validation
key_findings.summary: FP8 training achieves <0.25% relative loss error compared to BF16 baseline on models similar to DeepSeek-V2, validating feasibility for large-scale models with minimal performance degradation.

limitations.title: Quadratic Memory Complexity with Sequence Length
limitations.summary: Self-attention mechanisms require O(N²) memory for sequence length N, limiting context length scalability without sparse attention or memory optimizations.
limitations.details: Long-context extensions (e.g., 128K tokens) may require additional computational overhead or architectural modifications.

limitations.title: Hardware Dependency on Communication Overhead
limitations.summary: Efficient cross-node communication relies on InfiniBand and NVLink bandwidths, limiting scalability on clusters with lower interconnect performance.
limitations.details: Future hardware designs (e.g., unified IB-NVLink interfaces) could mitigate this dependency.

limitations.title: Training Stability with Low-Precision Formats
limitations.summary: FP8 training requires careful quantization strategies (e.g., fine-grained scaling) to avoid numerical instability, particularly with activation outliers.
limitations.details: Block-wise quantization of activations may introduce instability (discussed in Appendix B.2).

limitations.title: Expert Load Balancing in Inference
limitations.summary: Dynamic redundancy strategies for experts during inference are still under exploration, potentially introducing latency overhead for optimal routing computation.
limitations.details: Current deployment relies on periodic expert load statistics and redundant expert allocation.

equations.title: Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA) Key-Value Compression
equations.explanation: This set of equations describes the **Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA)** mechanism for compressing key-value pairs to reduce KV cache memory usage during inference. The process involves projecting the input hidden state `h_t` into a compressed latent vector `c_KV^t` using a down-projection matrix `W_DKV`. The compressed keys and values are then expanded back to the original dimension using up-projection matrices `W_UK` and `W_UV`, respectively. The keys are further split into two parts: a content-based key `k_C^t` and a RoPE (Rotary Positional Embedding)-carrying key `k_R^t`, which are concatenated to form the final key `k_t,i`. This approach significantly reduces memory overhead while maintaining performance comparable to standard Multi-Head Attention.

equations.title: DeepSeekMoE with Auxiliary-Loss-Free Load Balancing
latex: $g'_i,t = \begin{cases} s_i,t, & s_i,t \in \text{Top}_K(\{s_j,t | 1 \leq j \leq N_r\}, K_r), \ 0, & 	ext{otherwise}, \end{cases}$
$g'_i,t = \begin{cases} s_i,t + b_i, & s_i,t + b_i \in \text{Top}_K(\{s_j,t + b_j | 1 \leq j \leq N_r\}, K_r), \ 0, & 	ext{otherwise}, \end{cases}$
equations.explanation: This set of equations describes the **DeepSeekMoE with Auxiliary-Loss-Free Load Balancing** mechanism. The model uses a combination of shared experts and routed experts to process the input hidden state `u_t`. The output `h'^t` is computed by summing the contributions from shared experts and routed experts, weighted by gating values `g_i,t`. The gating values are derived from the affinity scores `s_i,t`, which are computed as the dot product of the input hidden state `u_t` and expert centroid vectors `e_i`, followed by a sigmoid activation. The auxiliary-loss-free load balancing strategy introduces bias terms `b_i` to adjust the affinity scores dynamically, ensuring balanced expert load without using auxiliary loss. This approach minimizes performance degradation while maintaining computational efficiency.

equations.title: Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) Training Objective
equations.explanation: This set of equations describes the **Multi-Token Prediction (MTP)** training objective. The MTP mechanism predicts multiple future tokens at each position by sequentially processing additional tokens. For each prediction depth `k`, the input `h'_{k,i}` is formed by concatenating the normalized hidden state `h_{k-1,i}` from the previous depth and the embedding of the next token `Emb(t_{i+k})`. This combined representation is processed by a Transformer block `TRM_k` to produce the output representation `h_{k,i}`. The shared output head `OutHead` then computes the probability distribution for the next token `P_{k,i+k+1}`. The cross-entropy loss `L_{k,MTP}` is computed for each prediction depth, and the overall MTP loss `L_{MTP}` is the weighted average of these losses across all depths. This approach enhances data efficiency and enables better planning of future token representations.

equations.title: Fine-Grained Quantization for FP8 Training
equations.explanation: This set of equations describes the **Fine-Grained Quantization** strategy for FP8 training. The quantization process involves scaling the input tensor `h_t` or weight matrix `W` to fit within the representable range of the FP8 format. Traditional methods scale the entire tensor or matrix to the maximum representable value of FP8, which can lead to quantization errors due to outliers. The fine-grained quantization method scales smaller groups of elements: a 1x128 tile for activations and a 128x128 block for weights. This approach mitigates the impact of outliers by adapting the scale to smaller groups, thereby improving quantization accuracy and reducing errors.

code_snippets.title: MultiHeadLatentAttention.py
code_snippets.code:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from torch.nn import functional as F

class MultiHeadLatentAttention(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, d_model, n_heads, d_kv, d_q, d_v, d_rope):
        super().__init__()
        self.d_model = d_model
        self.n_heads = n_heads
        self.d_kv = d_kv
        self.d_q = d_q
        self.d_v = d_v
        self.d_rope = d_rope

        # Projection matrices
        self.W_D_KV = nn.Linear(d_model, d_kv)  # Down-projection for KV
        self.W_U_K = nn.Linear(d_kv, n_heads * d_kv)  # Up-projection for keys
        self.W_U_V = nn.Linear(d_kv, n_heads * d_v)  # Up-projection for values
        self.W_K_R = nn.Linear(d_model, n_heads * d_rope)  # RoPE keys
        self.W_D_Q = nn.Linear(d_model, d_q)  # Down-projection for queries
        self.W_U_Q = nn.Linear(d_q, n_heads * d_q)  # Up-projection for queries
        self.W_Q_R = nn.Linear(d_q, n_heads * d_rope)  # RoPE queries
        self.W_O = nn.Linear(n_heads * d_q, d_model)  # Output projection

        # Initialize RoPE
        self.register_buffer('rope_theta', torch.tensor(10000.0))

    def forward(self, x):
        # x shape: (batch_size, seq_len, d_model)
        batch_size, seq_len, _ = x.shape

        # Down-project queries, keys, values
        c_Q = self.W_D_Q(x)  # (batch_size, seq_len, d_q)
        c_KV = self.W_D_KV(x)  # (batch_size, seq_len, d_kv)

        # Up-project keys and values
        K_C = self.W_U_K(c_KV).view(batch_size, seq_len, self.n_heads, self.d_kv)
        V_C = self.W_U_V(c_KV).view(batch_size, seq_len, self.n_heads, self.d_v)

        # RoPE keys
        K_R = self.W_K_R(x).view(batch_size, seq_len, self.n_heads, self.d_rope)
        K_R = self.apply_rope(K_R)

        # Concatenate compressed and RoPE keys
        K = torch.cat([K_C, K_R], dim=-1)  # (batch_size, seq_len, n_heads, d_kv + d_rope)

        # Down-project queries
        c_Q = self.W_D_Q(x)
        Q_C = self.W_U_Q(c_Q).view(batch_size, seq_len, self.n_heads, self.d_q)

        # RoPE queries
        Q_R = self.W_Q_R(c_Q).view(batch_size, seq_len, self.n_heads, self.d_rope)
        Q_R = self.apply_rope(Q_R)

        # Concatenate compressed and RoPE queries
        Q = torch.cat([Q_C, Q_R], dim=-1)  # (batch_size, seq_len, n_heads, d_q + d_rope)

        # Compute attention scores
        attn_scores = torch.matmul(Q, K.transpose(-2, -1)) / (self.d_kv + self.d_rope) ** 0.5
        attn_probs = F.softmax(attn_scores, dim=-1)

        # Compute attention output
        V = V_C.transpose(1, 2)  # (batch_size, n_heads, seq_len, d_v)
        output = torch.matmul(attn_probs, V)  # (batch_size, seq_len, n_heads, d_v)

        # Concatenate heads and project output
        output = output.transpose(1, 2).reshape(batch_size, seq_len, -1)
        output = self.W_O(output)

        return output

    def apply_rope(self, x):
        # Apply Rotary Positional Embedding (RoPE)
        seq_len, n_heads, d_rope = x.shape[0], x.shape[1], x.shape[2]
        theta = self.rope_theta
        pos = torch.arange(seq_len, device=x.device).float()
        inv_freq = 1.0 / (theta ** (torch.arange(0, d_rope, 2, device=x.device).float() / d_rope))
        t = pos[:, None] * inv_freq[None, :]
        cos = torch.cos(t)
        sin = torch.sin(t)

metadata.title: DeepSeek-V3 Technical Report
metadata.abstract: We present DeepSeek-V3, a strong Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language model with 671B total parameters with 37B activated for each token. To achieve efficient inference and cost-effective training, DeepSeek-V3 adopts Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) and DeepSeekMoE architectures, which were thoroughly validated in DeepSeek-V2. Furthermore, DeepSeek-V3 pioneers an auxiliary-loss-free strategy for load balancing and sets a multi-token prediction training objective for stronger performance. We pre-train DeepSeek-V3 on 14.8 trillion diverse and high-quality tokens, followed by Supervised Fine-Tuning and Reinforcement Learning stages to fully harness its capabilities. Comprehensive evaluations reveal that DeepSeek-V3 outperforms other open-source models and achieves performance comparable to leading closed-source models. Despite its excellent performance, DeepSeek-V3 requires only 2.788M H800 GPU hours for its full training. In addition, its training process is remarkably stable. Throughout the entire training process, we did not experience any irrecoverable loss spikes or perform any rollbacks.
